trigger_condition: the CLI option-to-property wiring for the three newly added disconnect flags is never exercised through Commander's actual argument parser, only the orchestrator function they call is unit-tested directly with hand-built target objects
guard_snippet: a CLI-level assertion like the existing one for --codex-desktop: `await createProxyCommand().parseAsync(['disconnect', '--claude-desktop'], { from: 'user' }); expect(disconnectTargets).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ targets: { claudeDesktop: true, vscode: false, vscodeClaudeCode: false, codexDesktop: false } });`
potential_consequence: if the option flag string ('--claude-desktop', '--vscode', '--vscode-claude-code') and the destructured property name (opts.claudeDesktop, opts.vscode, opts.vscodeClaudeCode) ever drift apart (typo, rename, commander kebab-case mismatch), `codemie proxy disconnect --claude-desktop` would silently do nothing (falls through to the 'select a target' no-op path) and no test would fail, since disconnect-orchestrator.test.ts calls disconnectTargets({targets:{claudeDesktop:true}}) directly, bypassing the CLI parser entirely, and connect-wiring.test.ts only exercises this pattern for --codex-desktop
consumer: the `codemie proxy disconnect --claude-desktop|--vscode|--vscode-claude-code` CLI entry point defined at src/cli/commands/proxy/index.ts:316-337
evidence: read src/cli/commands/proxy/__tests__/connect-wiring.test.ts in full: only one test ('routes `proxy disconnect --codex-desktop` to disconnectTargets', line 205) drives the disconnect command through createProxyCommand().parseAsync and asserts the resulting disconnectTargets call; no equivalent test exists for --claude-desktop, --vscode or --vscode-claude-code on the disconnect command (the analogous pattern is only present for the connect command's --vscode flag at line 167). All new-flag coverage in disconnect-orchestrator.test.ts (lines 86-180 of the diff) calls disconnectTargets({targets:{...}}) directly, never through Commander option parsing.
